record.summary: Kenya's national AI strategy for 2025-2030, built on three pillars (digital infrastructure, data, and research and innovation) and four enablers, one of them governance. The governance goal plans a national AI and emerging technologies policy, local ethical and safety standards implemented through conformity assessment, safety audits and technical regulations, a national AI risk and safety institute, regulatory sandboxes and, as AI matures, an AI and Other Emerging Technologies Act. The ethics goal plans a mandatory ethical impact assessment for public-sector AI, accountable procurement guidelines and a complaints and redress mechanism.
record.notes: Dated March 2025; the ministry announced that it would launch the strategy on 27 March 2025 at the Kenyatta International Convention Center. Developed by the National AI Working Group and Steering Committee with support from Germany's Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development, the EU-funded Digital Transformation Center Kenya implemented by GIZ, Canada's IDRC and the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. For each goal it sets objectives, flagship projects, outcomes and key performance indicators.
record.scope_note: Mainly a strategy for AI infrastructure, data, research and innovation, skills and investment, with governance and ethics among its enablers; included as Kenya's national AI strategy, which plans AI risk and safety frameworks and a national AI risk and safety institute.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the ministry's news item of 25 March 2025 announcing the launch (ict.go.ke, 16 Oct 2026) and the OECD.AI-hosted PDF of the strategy (91 pages, 11 Oct 2026). The ministry page confirms the title, the ministry and the launch date of 27 March 2025, announced in advance; it does not link the strategy document, and the PDF the archiver took from its links is an unrelated notice of cybersecurity job opportunities. The OECD-hosted PDF confirms the title, the March 2025 date, the Cabinet Secretary's foreword and the content summarised. No copy of the strategy on a Kenyan government site is stored.

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding strategy for 2025-2030, launched by the ministry in March 2025 (announced for 27 March 2025). Its implementation period runs to 2030 and nothing stored shows it replaced or withdrawn; the draft AI and Other Emerging Technologies Policy of July 2026 (KE-02, separate record) builds on it rather than replacing it. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.scope_reasoning: A national AI strategy with an AI risk and safety framework, a planned risk and safety institute and ethics measures; in scope, with a scope_note because its main focus is infrastructure, data, research and adoption.
judgment.date_reasoning: The strategy's cover reads 'March 2025'. The ministry's news item of 25 March 2025 announces the launch for 27 March 2025, before the event; no stored source confirms that the launch took place on that day, so 2025-03 is kept and the day goes in the notes as the announced launch date.
judgment.topics_reasoning: safety institute (5.2.3 national AI risk and safety institute); evaluation & testing (conformity assessment schemes and safety audits, 5.2.2); public-sector use (7.1.1 mandatory ethical impact assessment for the public sector, 7.1.2 procurement guidelines); accountability & liability (7.1.4 complaints and redress mechanism; transparency and accountability principle); international cooperation (5.4.2).

open_questions: No copy of the strategy on a Kenyan government site is among the stored files: the ministry's launch page does not link it, and the record rests on the copy hosted by OECD.AI.
